strengths: Novel extension of model soups and linear mode connectivity (LMC) to self-supervised learning objectives, demonstrating for the first time that models inter-trained with diverse SSL losses (e.g., MAE, MoCoV3, MMCR) remain linearly connectable and benefit from parameter averaging.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation covering multiple out-of-distribution benchmarks (ImageNet-C, LAION-C, ImageNet-A/R/V2/HR) and 21 visual tasks across the VTAB benchmark under both clean and corrupted settings.

Introduction of 'Self-Seasoning', a creative and fully unsupervised method for determining mixing coefficients via kNN prediction entropy minimization, supported with concise algorithmic implementation.
Clear conceptual motivation and well-executed figures (notably Figure 2 illustrating ternary interpolation across distinct SSL objectives).
weaknesses: Modest performance improvements in several standard settings: in Table 1 (in-distribution ImageNet) and Table 4 (VTAB clean/mean), gains over the 'Continued SSL + Supervised Soup' baseline are thin (often within 0.1% to 0.8%).

The large gains observed in Section 4.3 rely on access to unlabeled data from the test corruption distribution (ImageNet-C / LAION-C), which represents a distinct data-regime advantage over standard supervised soups.

Self-Seasoning (Table 5) exhibits inconsistent performance across tasks, underperforming simple uniform averaging on several datasets (e.g., Clevr-Count dropping from 27.4% to 17.5%, and sNORB-Elev dropping from 23.1% to 19.0%).

strengths: Original and interesting conceptual advance: demonstrates for the first time that linear mode connectivity (LMC) can hold between models branched from the same initialization and trained using fundamentally different self-supervised learning objectives (reconstruction via MAE, instance-contrastive via MoCoV3, and dimension-contrastive via MMCR).

Introduction of 'Self-Seasoning', a neat unsupervised recipe for optimizing mixture coefficients using kNN prediction entropy on unlabeled target samples, eliminating the reliance on labeled validation sets.
Extensive empirical evaluation spanning standard ImageNet robustness suites (ImageNet-A/R/C, LAION-C) and transfer across 21 visual tasks in VTAB under clean and corrupted conditions.
Clear presentation and intuitive visualizations (e.g., ternary mixing plots in Figure 2 and conceptual flow diagrams in Figures 1 and 3).
weaknesses: Fairness and baselines in the test-distribution experiment (§4.3): While the gains on ImageNet-C (+3.5%) and LAION-C (+7%) are impressive, this transductive/UDA setting provides Self-Soup with access to 100K steps of unlabeled target corruption data. Table 2 lacks a 'Continued SSL + Supervised Soup' baseline inter-trained directly on the corrupted target data, making it difficult to disentangle the benefit of target-domain continued SSL from the benefit of souping diverse SSL runs.

Modest gains in standard in-distribution and natural transfer settings: When inter-training only on in-domain training data (Table 1), improvements over standard supervised soups and continued SSL baselines are narrow (e.g., ImageNet-Val 79.35% vs. 79.34% greedy, 79.11% vs. 79.12% uniform).
Incomplete Appendix C: Section C ('Data and Code') contains empty section headers ('Data.' and 'Code.') with no content or repository details provided.

Computational overhead: Generating diverse ingredients across multiple distinct SSL frameworks and hyperparameter configurations incurs non-trivial training FLOPs compared to standard supervised fine-tuning sweeps.

strengths: Empirical demonstration of linear mode connectivity (LMC) across distinct SSL families: Showing that checkpoints inter-trained from a shared stock with fundamentally different self-supervised objectives (pixel reconstruction with MAE, instance contrastive with MoCo-v3, and dimension contrastive with MMCR) can be interpolated in weight space without barrier is novel and intriguing.

Comprehensive experimental scope: The manuscript systematically evaluates in-distribution performance (ImageNet-1K), a wide array of distribution shifts (ImageNet-A/R/C/V2/HR, LAION-C), and transfer learning across 21 diverse VTAB benchmark datasets.

Fair baseline comparison: The inclusion of 'Continued SSL + Supervised Soup' ensures that reported performance gains over standard supervised soups are properly disentangled from the computational benefits of extra self-supervised compute.
weaknesses: Incomplete manuscript content: Appendix C ('Data and Code') consists only of blank subheadings ('Data.' and 'Code.' with no text), reflecting an unfinished draft.

Marginal gains in standard settings and lack of statistical error bars: On in-distribution ImageNet-Val (Table 1), Self-Soup (79.35% greedy / 79.11% uniform) is practically indistinguishable from standard Supervised Soup (79.34% greedy / 79.12% uniform). On VTAB (Table 4), the overall accuracy improvements are marginal (~0.5–0.8%). Because no error bars, standard deviations, or multi-seed runs are reported, it is difficult to determine whether these differences are statistically significant.

Instability and underperformance of Self-Seasoning: In Table 5, the proposed unsupervised entropy-minimization mixing (Self-Seasoning) frequently underperforms a naive uniform average (e.g., Clevr-Count drops from 27.4% to 17.5%, and sNORB-Elev drops from 23.1% to 19.0%), and severely lags behind supervised seasoning and individual best ingredients on structured tasks. The learned weights also exhibit heavy collapse toward single ingredients, suggesting that neighbor entropy is a noisy surrogate for task accuracy.

Primary robustness gains rely on transductive access to the test distribution: The most substantial performance gains (+3.5% on ImageNet-C, +7% on LAION-C) require inter-training directly on the unlabeled target corruption distribution. In practical out-of-distribution deployments where corruptions and shifts are unforeseen, the expected benefit is much less pronounced.

strengths: Conceptual novelty: The paper is the first to demonstrate that linear mode connectivity (LMC) holds between ingredients trained via fundamentally different self-supervised learning (SSL) paradigms (e.g., MAE, MoCoV3, MMCR, LeJEPA), expanding the scope of model soups beyond supervised fine-tuning.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: Experiments span multiple axes including standard ImageNet validation, 7 out-of-distribution ImageNet benchmarks (ImageNet-C, LAION-C, ImageNet-A/R/V2/ReaL/HR), and all 21 VTAB tasks evaluated under both clean and corrupted settings.

Effective adaptation without supervision: The proposed Self-Seasoning method offers an unsupervised way to optimize mixture coefficients using kNN entropy minimization, demonstrating strong performance in few-shot regimes compared to full fine-tuning.

Practical robustness benefits: Demonstrates substantial OOD robustness gains (+3.5% on ImageNet-C, +7.0% on LAION-C) when shift-aware unlabeled data is available for inter-training, achieving performance competitive with or complementary to test-time adaptation (SAR) without incurring any test-time computational overhead.
Clear writing, engaging presentation, and well-designed visualizations (e.g., Figures 1, 2, and 3).
weaknesses: Marginal in-distribution improvements: On standard in-distribution metrics (e.g., ImageNet-Val in Table 1 or clean VTAB benchmarks in Table 4), the performance gains of Self-Souping over Continued SSL + Supervised Soup or standard Model Soups are relatively narrow (e.g., ~0.1% on IN-Val).

Transductive setup clarification: The most impressive gains (+3.5% on IN-C and +7% on LAION-C) rely on inter-training on the target corruption distribution. While evaluating disjoint splits appropriately addresses data contamination, this places the method closer to unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA); comparisons against established visual UDA methods are absent.

Incomplete sections in the manuscript: Section D on page 14 contains empty headings ('Data.' and 'Code.'), and the code URL in the abstract and Section 1 is an incomplete placeholder ('https://github.com/').

Computational overhead of ingredient generation: Inter-training multiple SSL runs (especially with diverse architectures/losses) followed by multiple fine-tuning sweeps adds significant training FLOPs compared to standard fine-tuning soup baselines.

strengths: Novel extension of linear mode connectivity (LMC) and model soups across disparate self-supervised learning objectives (e.g., combining pixel reconstruction like MAE, instance contrastive like MoCoV3, and dimension contrastive like MMCR/LeJEPA).
Strong empirical improvements on robustness benchmarks (ImageNet-C and LAION-C), demonstrating that self-supervised inter-training provides diverse and resilient parameter trajectories.

Introduction of Self-Seasoning, an intuitive and practical unsupervised mixing technique that optimizes ingredient mixture weights via nearest-neighbor entropy minimization without requiring labeled validation sets.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation spanning standard ImageNet test splits, 21 VTAB classification tasks across multiple corruption types, and comparisons with relevant baselines including Model Ratatouille and test-time adaptation (SAR).
weaknesses: Performance improvements on in-distribution evaluations (such as ImageNet-Val, ReaL, and V2 in Table 1) are marginal (within ~0.1-0.2%) compared to the Continued SSL baseline and standard supervised soups.

The test-distribution inter-training setup in Section 4.3 assumes advance access to the target shifted data distribution, which frames the problem similarly to unsupervised domain adaptation rather than purely post-hoc model merging.
The manuscript contains unfinished placeholders in the appendix (Appendix D 'Data and Code' has empty headers) and an incomplete GitHub link in the abstract.

A detailed computational budget comparison (e.g., total GPU hours required for inter-training across multiple SSL objectives vs. standard soups and multi-task SSL) is missing, which is important for understanding the practical trade-offs.

strengths: Novel exploration of Linear Mode Connectivity (LMC) across SSL algorithms: Demonstrating that LMC holds between models trained with fundamentally distinct self-supervised paradigms (masked autoencoding via MAE, instance contrastive via MoCoV3, and dimension contrastive via MMCR/LeJEPA) from a shared stock is an interesting empirical finding (Figures 2 and 5).

Comprehensive empirical scope: The paper evaluates across a wide range of settings, including 8 ImageNet-1K distribution shift benchmarks, 21 VTAB transfer tasks, comparisons with test-time adaptation (SAR) and Model Ratatouille, and few-shot classification setups.

Unsupervised mixture optimization idea: The proposed 'Self-Seasoning' method explores learning mixture coefficients without labels by optimizing a nearest-neighbor prediction entropy loss, extending the post-hoc soup weighting literature to the unsupervised regime.
weaknesses: Misleading attribution of performance gains: The abstract and introduction highlight substantial robustness gains (+3.5% on ImageNet-C and +7% on LAION-C). However, Table 2 reveals that almost all of this improvement comes from exposing the model to the unlabeled shifted distribution via continued SSL (Continued SSL + Soup on IN-C achieves 35.09%, while Self-Soup achieves 35.72%, a net improvement of only +0.63%). Attributing the entire gain from shift exposure to 'Self-Souping' is misleading.

Marginal improvements over existing baselines: On standard benchmarks where shift data is not leaked into inter-training, the gains are marginal. On ImageNet-Val (Table 1), Self-Soup improves over standard Supervised Soup by only +0.07% (79.41% vs 79.34%), and over Continued SSL + Supervised Soup by +0.03%. On VTAB (Table 4), the average gain across 21 datasets is similarly minor (+0.5% over uniform supervised soup).

Complete absence of error bars or statistical significance: Across all tables (Tables 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9), results are reported without standard deviations, confidence intervals, or repeated runs across random seeds. Given that reported margins are frequently between 0.05% and 0.5%, it is unclear whether these differences are statistically significant.

Potential degeneracies and validation of Self-Seasoning: Optimizing feature representations to minimize kNN entropy without labels (Eq. 3) risks collapsing representations into dense arbitrary clusters. Furthermore, inspection of the learned coefficients (Table 8) shows heavy collapse onto a single ingredient (MMCR global+local or MoCoV3) across most tasks, rather than nuanced task-dependent mixing.

Incomplete presentation and broken references: Appendix D ('Data and Code') contains empty headers with no content. Multiple text references point to the wrong tables/figures (e.g., Section 4.2/4.3 and Table 2 refer to 'Tab. 7' when meaning Table 1, and Section 4.6 refers to 'Tab. 4' for few-shot results when meaning Fig. 4 / Table 9).
